ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the pentagon in order is P-Q-R-S-T. P, U, R are on the same vertical line segment, and U is located between P and R; Q is on the right side, connected with P and R to form triangle PQR; T and S are on the left side, connected with P, U, R through line segments, dividing the pentagon into four triangles PQR, PTU, SUT, RSU. Reasoning: Let the side length of the equilateral triangle PQR be a, then PQ=QR=PR=a, and the perimeter of triangle PQR is 3a. From the figure it can be seen that U is on PR; also because PTU, SUT, RSU are congruent isosceles triangles, and in the correspondence PU, ST, RU are the bases, so PU=ST=RU. Since PU+RU=PR=a, PU=RU=a/2, and ST=a/2. Let the common leg length of these small isosceles triangles be x, then PT=TU=SU=RS=x. The perimeters of the four triangles are equal, therefore the perimeter of triangle PTU is also equal to 3a, thus 2x+a/2=3a, solving gives x=5a/4. The perimeter of pentagon PQRST is PQ+QR+RS+ST+TP=a+a+x+a/2+x=5a. Therefore its ratio with the perimeter 3a of triangle PQR is 5a:3a=5:3.

raw_record.question_text: The Pentagon $P Q R S T$ is divided into four triangles with equal perimeters. The triangle $P Q R$ is equilateral. $P T U$, $S U T$, and $R S U$ are congruent isosceles triangles. method.method_draft: Let the side length of the equilateral triangle PQR be a, so PQ=QR=PR=a and the perimeter of PQR is 3a. From the diagram, U lies on PR, and the top and bottom congruent isosceles triangles PTU and RSU use PU and RU as their bases; hence PU=RU=a/2. The middle congruent isosceles triangle SUT has base ST corresponding to PU and RU, so ST=a/2. Let the common leg length of the small isosceles triangles be x; then PT=TU=SU=RS=x. Since every small triangle has the same perimeter as PQR, for triangle PTU we have 2x+a/2=3a, giving x=5a/4. The pentagon perimeter is PQ+QR+RS+ST+TP=a+a+x+a/2+x=5a. Therefore the ratio to the perimeter of PQR is 5a:3a=5:3.

method.method_draft: Normalize by the common triangle perimeter p. Since PQR is equilateral and has perimeter p, each side of PQR is p/3, so PR=p/3. From the diagram and congruence, PU and UR are corresponding bases of the top and bottom isosceles triangles, so PU=UR and PU+UR=PR; hence each small base is p/6. The middle triangle SUT is congruent with base ST corresponding to PU and UR, so ST=p/6. Instead of solving for each slanted side, observe that the three left outer pentagon sides PT, ST, and SR consist of two equal legs plus one corresponding base, exactly the side-length multiset of any one of the congruent isosceles triangles. Therefore PT+ST+SR=p. The remaining two outer pentagon sides are PQ and QR, each p/3. Thus the pentagon perimeter is p+p/3+p/3=5p/3, while the perimeter of PQR is p, so the ratio is 5:3.

The outer boundary of the pentagon consists of PQ, QR, RS, ST, and TP.

Reasoning: Let the common perimeter of each of the four triangles be p. Since triangle PQR is equilateral and has perimeter p, each of its sides is p/3, so PR = p/3.
